why: Fabricated quote on the wrong page, plus a false consequence. (1) The claimed sentence does not exist on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md in any form. Fetched copy: 567 lines, 60,850 bytes, md5 ad63081821d6d5c0ad82519f183a3c0f. `grep -in skill` yields exactly two hits — line 445 (".claude/skills/" in the live-reload table) and line 507 (strictPluginOnlyCustomization) — neither a rule row, and the page contains no table of the claimed three-column shape. Its "## Tool-specific permission rules" section (line 160) has exactly seven subsections: Bash, PowerShell, Read and Edit, WebFetch, MCP, Agent (subagents), Cd. No Skill subsection, no `Skill(` anywhere. The genuine contract lives on a DIFFERENT page, skills.md § "Restrict Claude's skill access" (lines 603-627), as a fenced code block containing `Skill(commit)` / `Skill(review-pr *)` / `Skill(deploy *)` followed at line 627 by "Permission syntax: `Skill(name)` for exact match, `Skill(name *)` for prefix match with any arguments." The finding presents an invented markdown table row as a verbatim quote from a page that never carried it. (2) The consequence is false and names the wrong subsystem. `parseClaudeRuleString` lives in `pi-harness/` and serves the Pi harness, which has NO `Skill` tool binding at all: `pi-harness/harness-tool-descriptor.ts` binds only `skill_validate` (:136, :271) and `read_skill_resource` (:184, :317); Pi materializes skill content into the turn via `materializeRuntimeSkillInvocation` rather than dispatching a `Skill` tool call. On the other backend, `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1118` places `Skill` in `disallowedTools` unconditionally: `const disallowedTools: string[] = ['EnterPlanMode', 'ExitPlanMode', 'AskUserQuestion', 'Skill'];`. So no `Skill` tool call exists in either runtime for a deny rule to gate — nothing is "silently granted" that a supported rule form would have denied. (3) It is also not silent: the `default:` branch returns `inert('claude_rule.unmatched_form', 'Permission <action> rule "…" uses a specifier form no permission check matches; the rule is ignored.')`, and that diagnostic is consumed at `managed-policy.ts:1017-1026` and `permissions-config.ts:529`. (4) Not one of the nine owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (checked; the nearest skill row, `SkillMetadata.disallowedTools`, sits in §2 and is a different symbol — itself an instance of the §4 shape-4 trap this finding also falls into).
correctedState: The mechanical half of the code claim is accurate; the citation and the consequence are not. Accurate: `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/claude-permission-rules.ts` has no `Skill` case (`grep -an Skill` on the file returns zero hits); its switch covers Bash, PowerShell, Read/Edit, Write/NotebookEdit/Glob, WebFetch, Agent, Cd, then `default:`. `Skill(deploy *)` carries no `param:` colon, so `PARAM_SPECIFIER` misses and it reaches the `inert('claude_rule.unmatched_form', …)` at lines 378-381. There is no `skill` matcher kind in `CompiledMatcher` — the kinds are tool, bash, bashPattern, powershell, path, pathGlob, cdPath, host, mcp, agent, parameter, at permission-dsl.ts lines 77-88 (the finding cites 76-87, off by one). Wrong: the doc page. `Skill(name)` / `Skill(name *)` is specified on skills.md lines 616-627, not permissions.md, and not as a table row — the finding's "quote" is fabricated. Wrong: the consequence. Neither backend exposes a `Skill` tool that such a rule would gate. Pi binds only `skill_validate` and `read_skill_resource` (harness-tool-descriptor.ts:136/184/271/317) and injects skill content directly; the Claude Agent SDK backend hard-blocks the SDK `Skill` tool at claude-agent.ts:1118. Skill invocation in this fork is gated by source enablement, `disable-model-invocation`, and path gating — a different subsystem from the tool-permission DSL. A correctly-scoped version of this observation would read: "Nessy does not model skill invocation as a permission-gated `Skill` tool, so Claude's `Skill(name)` name-matching rules have no surface to bind to; an imported rule is diagnosed as `claude_rule.unmatched_form` rather than applied." That is a design difference in how skills are dispatched, not a silent grant, and its doc contract is skills.md, not permissions.md.
